title: zazzle-csharp-indexer deployment diagram
description: How zazzle-csharp-indexer runs on a developer's machine: one self-contained executable, started as a stdio server per agent session, a shared daemon per user that zazzled also queries for terse C# views, and a short-lived hook per tool call. Nothing runs anywhere else.

sources.symbol: Build the C# indexer for both CPU types

nodes.name: Developer's machine
nodes.description: macOS (arm64 or x64) or Linux (x64 or arm64); the release builds these four. Everything below runs here as the same user.

nodes.name: Coding agent's client (for example Claude Code)
nodes.description: Starts zazzle-csharp-indexer serve and, where init found zazzled, zazzled mcp as stdio MCP servers per session, and runs zazzle-csharp-indexer hook before Bash, Grep, Glob and Read calls once init has configured the project.

nodes.name: Developer's terminal
nodes.description: Runs zazzle-csharp-indexer init in a project and zazzle-csharp-indexer report.

nodes.name: zazzle-csharp-indexer serve
nodes.description: One per MCP session: pipes standard input and output to the daemon, or serves in process with --no-daemon, ZAZZLE_INDEXER_NO_DAEMON=1 or when no daemon can be used.

nodes.name: zazzle-csharp-indexer daemon
nodes.description: One per state directory (per user by default), started detached by the first serve or zazzled that finds none, holding the engine, watchers and indexes; serves every client of daemon.sock and exits after the idle period.
nodes.condition: Unless every client serves in process

nodes.name: zazzled (macos/rust/zazzled/)
nodes.description: zazzle's daemon, another tool in this repository and the agents' front door for reading, searching and editing files. init registers zazzled mcp as the project's zazzle MCP server when it finds zazzled beside the indexer or on PATH. When zazzle reads a .cs file, zazzled connects to daemon.sock, starting the indexer daemon if nothing answers, sends the hello line and calls the view tool over MCP.

nodes.name: zazzle-csharp-indexer hook
nodes.description: One short-lived process per Bash, Grep, Glob or Read call; decides by exit code and appends to the usage log.
nodes.condition: In projects where zazzle-csharp-indexer init has run

nodes.name: zazzle-csharp-indexer init and report
nodes.description: One-shot commands: init writes the project's .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json, naming the indexer and the zazzled it finds; report reads the usage log.

nodes.name: State directory
nodes.description: store.db (SQLite, WAL), usage.jsonl and usage.jsonl.1, daemon.sock and an optional config.json, in ~/Library/Application Support/zazzle-csharp-indexer, $XDG_STATE_HOME/zazzle-csharp-indexer or ZAZZLE_INDEXER_STATE_DIR.

nodes.name: git
nodes.description: Child processes for work-tree checks, listings, ignore checks, log, blame and grep -P; must be on PATH.

nodes.name: rg (ripgrep)
nodes.description: Child process for search patterns .NET rejects, and for run when the agent asks for it.

nodes.name: Git work trees (the roots)
nodes.description: The source files the index reads and watches. zazzle-csharp-indexer's own code does not write them; only run with run.unrestricted can run a program that does.

artifacts.name: zazzle-csharp-indexer (single-file executable)
artifacts.description: dotnet publish src -c Release -r <rid>: self-contained, single file, ReadyToRun, native libraries included, not Developer ID signed. For macOS it is gzipped per CPU type into the release tarball and the zazzle Homebrew formula expands the matching one on install; for Linux it is in zazzle-linux-<arch>.tar.gz (delivery.json).

relationships.description: Started detached, by serve through /bin/sh with nohup or by zazzled.
Runs as its own process; how it starts is recorded in macos/rust/zazzled/.
MCP: newline-delimited JSON-RPC on standard input and output.
PreToolUse event as JSON on standard input; exit code 0 or 2.
MCP on the standard input and output of zazzled mcp, which init registers as the zazzle server.
Unix socket daemon.sock in the state directory: hello line, then MCP.
Unix socket daemon.sock: hello line with the version and roots, then MCP tools/call of view.
Its own store connection and log when serving in process.
Reads files; FSEvents (macOS) or FileSystemWatcher (elsewhere) on each root.
Spawned with an argument list and a timeout, never through a shell.
